findings: Electrical alternans with a swinging heart

echoTasks.find: Large circumferential echo free space persisting through the cycle, no chamber collapse yet
Swinging heart with fibrin strands and preserved caval collapse on sniff
Normal chamber sizes with an echo free space around the heart in the apical window

exam.general: Middle aged woman, comfortable at rest, mild tachypnoea, no distress lying at 30 degrees
exam.jvp: Mildly raised 5 cm, falls normally on inspiration
exam.other: No pulsus paradoxus on careful cuff check, lungs clear, no lymphadenopathy felt
exam.precordium: Impalpable apex beat, cardiac dullness extended beyond the apex
exam.pulse: Regular 95, normal volume, no paradox felt

history.a: One month of low grade fever with evening rise, dry cough, dull central chest ache
Breathless on climbing stairs for two weeks, can still lie flat
No wheeze, no sputum, weight down 3 kg with poor appetite
Husband completed pulmonary tuberculosis treatment last year
No diabetes, no hypertension, two children delivered normally
Homemaker, vegetarian diet, no smoking, chulha smoke exposure in the past

keyPoints: Confirm tuberculosis with pericardial fluid analysis where drainage is indicated, plus sputum molecular testing
Start antitubercular treatment under the national programme with adherence support once the diagnosis is firm
Admit for observation with serial echo, as large effusions can progress to tamponade without warning
Avoid NSAIDs as monotherapy and avoid diuretics that lower preload in a large effusion
Plan steroid review per the ESC pericardial guideline only where specifically indicated, with diabetes and ulcer checks
management.model: Tuberculosis workup with programme linked treatment, inpatient echo surveillance, and preload preserving care

sources: ESC guideline on pericardial disease, in own words
National tuberculosis elimination programme guidance on extrapulmonary disease, in own words
stem: A 45 year old homemaker from Bihar with a treated tuberculosis contact at home presents with a month of evening fever and two weeks of exertional breathlessness. Heart sounds are muffled without a rub, and the ECG shows low voltage with alternans.
teaching: Low voltage with electrical alternans plus muffled sounds means fluid around the heart until proved otherwise
Large means above 20 mm, usually with a swinging heart, and collapse may still be absent
Tuberculosis is the leading cause of large effusions in India, so contact history matters as much as the echo
Large effusions need inpatient watch because tamponade can follow quickly
title: Large tuberculous pericardial effusion without tamponade
